entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.
Hon'ble Manish Kumar Nigam,J.
1.

The petitioner has prayed for quashing of notice dated 22.5.2024 issued under Section 3E of the
National Highways Act, 1956, calling upon the petitioner to approach the Competent Authority for
obtaining compensation amount in respect of acquisition of his land comprising of Gata No. 305,
area 0.0950 hectare.

2.  On 23.7.2024, the following order was passed: -
"1.
The petitioner claims ownership over Gata No.305 measuring 0.1410 Hectare.

The area of acquired land of Gata No.305 is 0.0950 Hectare as per notice u/s 3-E of the Rampratap vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61603430/
1 National Highways Act, 1956.

entities.text: Rampratap vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
2. The case of the petitioner is that respondents are widening the road by taking land from one side only resulting in the entire land of the petitioner being taken over by respondents although the acquisition was of 0.0950 Hectare only.
3. Learned State Counsel to obtain instructions on the said aspect and clearly disclose how much land from the center of road is being taken over by the respondents in pursuance of the acquisition notifications.
4. List as fresh on 13.8.2024."
3.

On matter being taken up today, Sri Rajiv Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel, has placed on record written instructions received from Special Land Acquisition Officer, Banda dated 8.8.2024.
According to it, the acquisition has been made on both sides of the existing road.
The land of the petitioner as well as another plot of land bearing number 307 in front of the plot of the petitioner, had been utilized for construction of toll plaza.
The contention of the petitioner that the respondent had taken land only from one side, resulting in entire land of the petitioner being taken away, has been emphatically denied.
It is stated that still the petitioner is left with 0.046 hectare of land.
4. Counsel for the petitioner submits that the respondents be directed to demarcate petitioner's remaining land to set at rest the entire controversy.
5. Sri Rajiv Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel, is agreeable to the same.

6. Accordingly, the instant petition is disposed of by providing that the second respondent will constitute a team of revenue officials for demarcation of the remaining area of the petitioner measuring 0.046 hectare, within three weeks from the date of communication of the instant order.
The demarcation exercise shall be held in presence of the petitioner and officials of NHAI.

(Manish Kumar Nigam, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.) Order Date :- 13.8.2024 Jaideep/-
